channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: 0.7050: Australian Dollar stuck in a range as Iran risks offset hawkish RBA
item.description: The AUD/USD pair holds steady during the Asian session on Thursday and, for now, seems to have stalled the previous day's retracement slide from its highest level since June 5.

item.title: UK GDP expected to show moderate Q2 growth
item.description: The United Kingdom’s (UK) Office for National Statistics will release the preliminary estimate of the second-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on Thursday. Market analysts anticipate a 0.4% growth in the three months to June, after a modest 0.6% advance in the first quarter of 2026.

item.title: Canadian Dollar steadies as weak US Dollar offsets lower oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD remains steady after registering minor gains in the previous day, trading around 1.3940 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The currency pair moves within a narrow range as a weaker US Dollar (USD) balances out the impact of falling oil prices on the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: British Pound posts modest gains to near 1.3500 ahead of UK GDP data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges slightly higher to near 1.3500 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. The US Dollar (USD) softens against the British Pound (GBP) on a tame reading of the US inflation report.

item.title: United States Dollar Index stalls post-CPI bounce near 100.00 on receding Fed hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, continues its struggle to build on the momentum beyond the 100.00 psychological mark and edges lower during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7888 vs. 6.7882 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.7888 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7882 and 6.7470 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro advances as US Dollar weakens amid cooling Inflation
item.description: EUR/USD halts its three-day losing streak, trading around 1.1530 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The currency pair gains ground as the US Dollar (USD) faces challenges following the release of July's Consumer Price Index (CPI) report.

item.title: WTI declines below $82.50 as oil inventories rise far more than expected
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $82.45 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. WTI declines on a larger-than-expected build in US crude oil inventories. Traders will closely monitor the developments surrounding US-Iran talks for fresh impetus.

item.title: RBA's Kent: Cash rate hikes are achieving their intended impact
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Assistant Governor Chris Kent said on Thursday that interest rate hikes are producing the expected effect. Kent added that further rate increases possible if risks emerge.

item.title: Iran says no progress on interim peace deal with US — Reuters
item.description: The United States (US) and Iran remain at ​loggerheads over efforts to agree a permanent end to the war in the Middle East, Reuters reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Gold edges lower to near $4,400 as Iran-US tensions counter support from tame US inflation
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to around $4,400 during the early Asian session on Thursday, pressured by escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Commodities: Weaker Dollar lacks growth catalyst – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY says a less hawkish Fed has weakened the Dollar, but this has not translated into a broad commodity rally. Institutional investors remain sellers of metals and miners, while EM commodity sovereign debt continues to struggle and commodity FX buying has faded.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gives back half of what Tokyo bought
item.description: The Dollar has spent Wednesday grinding higher against the Yen with no headline to carry it, trading near 159.50 after a low just beneath 158.60 and a gain of under a tenth of a percent.

item.title: Pound Sterling runs out of room at the July high
item.description: Sterling spent the London morning building a case for a break and the rest of the session dismantling it, trading near 1.3495 after a high just short of 1.3550 and a loss of not quite a tenth of a percent.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: 50-day SMA caps sideways trading
item.description: The GBP/JPY holds firm on Wednesday at around 215.00, as neither buyers nor sellers are reluctant to open fresh directional bets amid fears of renewed intervention in the FX markets by US and Japanese authorities to propel the Yen.

item.title: Indonesia: BI succession supports Rupiah stability – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Radhika Rao reports that Indonesia’s onshore markets welcomed President Prabowo’s nomination of Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti as the next Bank Indonesia Governor.

item.title: Australian Dollar pulls back as inflation expectations loom
item.description: The Aussie Dollar ended Wednesday’s session with losses against the Greenback as US inflation data matched estimates, in both headline and core. Consequently, traders pushed back against rate hikes, though the AUD/USD faded the initial move and traded at 0.7061, down 0.07%.

item.title: Euro reverses from two-day high, fade US soft CPI move
item.description: The Euro reversed course after reaching a two-day high of 1.1563, following the release of a benign US inflation report for July, which triggered a repricing for a less “hawkish” Federal Reserve, throughout 2026.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Credit softness may spur PBoC easing – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao point out USD/CNY is stable around 6.75, with their model implying a slightly stronger PBoC fix.

item.title: Mexican Peso rallies to two-year high as soft CPI hits Fed bets
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) appreciates on Wednesday against the US Dollar (USD) to levels last seen in May 2024 following a decline in US inflation, as markets expected, softer-than-expected, which trims bets of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed) in its next meeting.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slips as Middle East uncertainty weighs on Kiwi
item.description: NZD/USD is trading near 0.5860, down over 0.30% on Wednesday and falling for the third consecutive day.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk builds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD closed little changed around 1.2800, with the S$NEER trading 1.7% above its mid-point and implying a 1.2760–1.2822 range.

item.title: Commodity FX: Growth constraints cap carry – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that a less hawkish Fed has weakened the Dollar but failed to spark a sustained bid in commodity FX such as Norwegian Krone (NOK), Australian Dollar (AUD) and Emerging Markets (EM) currencies Chilean Peso (CLP), South African Rand (ZAR) and Brazilian Real (BRL).

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bearish flag forms as bulls eye 0.8200
item.description: The USD/CHF pair edges higher by some 0.30% on Wednesday, refreshing ten-day highs of 0.8138, as the uptrend is poised to extend if it clears key resistance levels.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade and upside risk against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH has been confined to a tight range and expect the Dollar to trade between 6.7430 and 6.7530 in the near term.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms ahead of a packed session
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has extended its recovery on Wednesday following a Consumer Price Index (CPI) report that printed in line with forecasts. The US Dollar Index (DXY) has pushed back above the 100.00 mark, and the bid has broadened out against most majors heading into a data-heavy Thursday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG turns bullish, eyes 200-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price surges over 1.40% on Wednesday as the latest inflation report in the United States (US) showed that prices are cooling, on its way towards the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) goal of 2%. At the time of writing, the XAG/USD pair trades at $65.53 after reaching a daily high of $66.80.

item.title: Gold price shines above $4,400 as inflation dip fuels Fed relief
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) registers gains of over 1% on Wednesday as US inflation data aligns with estimates, easing the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) task of further tightening monetary policy. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) continues its downward trajectory.

item.title: Japanese Yen stumbles as US Dollar strengthens
item.description: USD/JPY is back around the mid-159.00s area, testing the day's highs after rebounding sharply from a low around the 158.60 level.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Fading bullish momentum puts focus on 1.1500 support
item.description: EUR/USD edges lower on Wednesday, reversing earlier gains as the US Dollar (USD) shrugs off in-line US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1521 after touching an intraday high of 1.1563.
